claims.claim_text: Hyzon operates a 110,000 sq ft fuel cell system manufacturing facility in Bolingbrook, IL (office, fuel cell system manufacturing, powertrain development, prototype build, test labs).
claims.source_quote: United States Bolingbrook, IL Office, fuel cell system manufacturing, powertrain development, software/controls engineering, prototype build, test labs - electrical systems/components, battery systems, and thermal management 110,000 Lease
claims.subject: Hyzon Motors Inc.
claims.extraction_notes: Fuel-cell manufacturing facility processing chemical/industrial inputs should be EPA-FRS registered. Absence would weaken the manufacturing-scale claim. Bolingbrook is the company headquarters and most material US facility.

claims.claim_text: Hyzon is a registered US heavy-duty truck OEM, assembling/converting Class 8 hydrogen fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs).
claims.source_quote: Hyzon is a global supplier of high-performance hydrogen fuel cell systems focused on providing zero-emission power to decarbonize the most demanding industries. We are commercializing our proprietary fuel cell technology through assembling and upfitting heavy duty ( HD ) hydrogen fuel cell electric vehicles ( FCEVs ).
claims.subject: Hyzon Motors Inc.
claims.extraction_notes: NHTSA vPIC registry should list Hyzon as a Truck or Incomplete Vehicle manufacturer if real US OEM operations exist. 'Incomplete Vehicle' would indicate glider/upfit business only, consistent with the upfit-services language. Anything weaker than 'Truck' weakens the OEM claim.

claims.claim_text: Hyzon reached a final resolution with the SEC on September 26, 2023 requiring payment of a $25.0 million civil penalty in three tranches ($8.5M within 30 days; $8.5M by Dec 31, 2024; $8.0M within 730 days).
claims.source_quote: On September 26, 2023, the Company announced a final resolution, subject to court approval, of the SEC s investigation. On that date, the SEC filed a complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of New York naming the Company, Craig Knight, the Company s former Chief Executive Officer and a former director, and Max C.B. Holthausen, a former managing director of the Company s European subsidiary, Hyzon Motors Europe B.V., as defendants. ... and would require the Company to pay a civil penalty of $ 25.0 million as follows: $ 8.5 million within 30 days of entry of the final judgment; (2) $ 8.5 million by December 31, 2024; and (3) $ 8.0 million within 730 days of entry of the final judgment.
claims.subject: Hyzon Motors Inc.
claims.extraction_notes: SEC enforcement action / settlement should be filed via 8-K and AAER. edgar_fts on Hyzon's own CIK adjudicates whether the settlement is on the docket. Authoritative independent registry would be SEC AAER (Accounting and Auditing Enforcement Releases) or SEC Litigation Releases — captured by EDGAR fulltext.

claims.claim_text: On January 23, 2024 Hyzon received a Nasdaq deficiency notice for non-compliance with the $1.00 Minimum Bid Price Rule on the Nasdaq Capital Market.
claims.source_quote: On January 23, 2024, the Company received a new letter from The Nasdaq Stock Market notifying the Company that it no longer complies with the Bid Price Rule for continued listing on The Nasdaq Capital Market. The Bid Price Rule requires listed securities to maintain a minimum bid price of $1.00 per share, and Nasdaq's Compliance Period Rule provides that a failure to meet the minimum bid price requirement exists if the deficiency continues for a period of 30 consecutive business days.
claims.subject: Hyzon Motors Inc.
claims.object_value: Nasdaq Capital Market (Bid Price Rule, sub-$1.00)
claims.extraction_notes: Listing-deficiency notice must be disclosed on 8-K Item 3.01. edgar_fts on Hyzon's CIK adjudicates the filing existence. Going-concern indicator material to short thesis.

claims.claim_text: Hyzon owns hydrogen fuel cell intellectual property co-developed with JS Horizon (Jiangsu Qingneng / Shanghai Qingneng Horizon) under the Horizon IP Agreement, including jointly-owned Background IP and provisional patent applications.
claims.source_quote: In January 2021, the Company entered into an intellectual property agreement (the Horizon IP Agreement ) with Jiangsu Qingneng New Energy Technologies Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Qingneng Horizon New Energy Ltd. (together, JS Horizon ) both of which are subsidiaries of the Company s ultimate parent, Horizon. Under the Horizon IP Agreement, JS Horizon assigned to the Company a joint ownership interest in certain intellectual property rights previously developed by JS Horizon ( Background IP ) ... the Company also grants JS Horizon a perpetual non-exclusive license under certain provisional patent applications (and any patents issuing therefrom)
claims.subject: Hyzon Motors Inc.
claims.extraction_notes: USPTO ODP adjudicates whether Hyzon (as opposed to its Chinese parent Horizon) actually holds granted US patents in fuel-cell technology. Low US-patent count would corroborate the short thesis that the IP largely lives at JS Horizon in China and the US entity is mostly an assembly/upfit operation.

claims.claim_text: Hyzon delivered 62 FCEVs in 2022 (China) generating $2.5M revenue; in 2023 US FCEV revenue collapsed to $0.3M from a single FCEV sale.
claims.source_quote: Revenue for the year ended December 31, 2023 was $0.3 million from sale of a FCEV in the U.S. Revenue for the year ended December 31, 2022 was $3.7 million and consists of $2.5 million from the sale of 62 FCEVs, $1.1 million from sales of fuel cell systems, and $0.1 million from upfit services.
claims.subject: Hyzon Motors Inc.
claims.extraction_notes: NREL adjudicates whether Hyzon-branded hydrogen refueling infrastructure exists in the US — necessary for any meaningful US FCEV fleet deployment. Absence of any Hyzon-affiliated H2 stations corroborates the near-zero US delivery volume ($0.3M revenue = 1 FCEV) and contradicts the company's headline 'back-to-base' commercial deployment narrative. Note: actual delivery counts (62 in China, 1 in US) are inside the financials and not separately registry-verifiable; NREL is the closest registry proxy for production-vehicle operational presence.

claims.claim_text: Hyzon is in legal dispute with Dutch customers Duurzaam Transport B.V. and H2 Transport B.V., who in January 2023 filed an attachment against Hyzon Europe in Dutch court alleging non-delivery of contracted trucks.
claims.source_quote: In January 2023, Duurzaam Transport B.V. and H2 Transport B.V., both private limited companies in the Netherlands and customers of the Company s European subsidiary, Hyzon Europe, filed an attachment with the local Dutch court. The initial attachment claimed that Hyzon Europe was liable for liquidated and consequential damages stemming from Hyzon Europe allegedly not delivering trucks as contracted.
claims.subject: Hyzon Europe
claims.object_value: Duurzaam Transport B.V. and H2 Transport B.V.

proposed_connector.name: kvk_nl.query_company_registry
proposed_connector.description: Dutch Chamber of Commerce (Kamer van Koophandel) business registry — adjudicates existence, registration date, status (active/dissolved/bankrupt), directors, and registered address of any Dutch BV / NV.
proposed_connector.rationale: When a company names a foreign counterparty (here, Dutch BV customers), the home-country business registry is the authoritative adjudicator of (a) the counterparty's existence and active status, (b) registered size proxies (employees, share capital), and (c) bankruptcy/dissolution flags. KvK is the Dutch federal registry equivalent to EDGAR — necessary because edgar_fts cannot find counterparties that do not file with the SEC.
proposed_connector.estimated_cost: free (open KvK Zoeken API) / paid tier for full extracts
proposed_connector.completeness: all Dutch-registered businesses (BV, NV, eenmanszaak, etc.)

claims.extraction_notes: Customer dispute is material because (i) it implies prior contracted-but-undelivered trucks recognized as revenue under earlier accounting, and (ii) the customer counterparties are non-US private BVs invisible to EDGAR. KvK adjudicates whether these are bona-fide trucking customers vs. shell entities — relevant to the prior SEC restatement narrative around 'fake customer contracts'.

claims.claim_text: Hyzon has substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern; as of Dec 31, 2023 had $112.3M unrestricted cash with $135.6M annual operating cash burn and accumulated deficit of $242.6M.
claims.source_quote: As of the date of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, the Company has concluded that substantial doubt exists about its ability to continue as a going concern as the Company believes that its existing financial resources are not sufficient to support planned operations for the next 12 months following the issuance date of these consolidated financial statements. ... Net cash used in operating activities was $ 135.6 million and $ 149.1 million for the years ended December 31, 2023 and 2022, respectively. As of December 31, 2023, the Company has $ 112.3 million in unrestricted cash and cash equivalents and $ 5.8 million in restricted cash. ... Accumulated deficit amounts to $ 242.6 million
claims.subject: Hyzon Motors Inc.
claims.object_value: $112.3M cash vs $135.6M annual burn; accumulated deficit $242.6M
claims.extraction_notes: Going-concern + ~10 months runway implies an imminent dilutive equity raise. sec_filings.list_filings_by_form adjudicates the registry-side evidence of post-going-concern financing activity (S-1/S-3/424B prospectus filings, ATM agreements via 8-K). Heavy filing cadence of these forms post-Mar-2024 (filing date of 10-K) corroborates the burn trajectory and indicates dilution pressure on the short-leg.
